extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating language agents in real-world planning with multiple constraints, focusing on travel planning scenarios. It provides a rich sandbox environment with around four million data entries, various tools for accessing information, and 1,225 meticulously curated planning intents and reference plans.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su
extraction.publisher: Fudan University, The Ohio State University, The Pennsylvania State University, Meta AI
extraction.citeAs: Xie, J., Zhang, K., Chen, J., Zhu, T., Lou, R., Tian, Y., Xiao, Y., & Su, Y. (2024). TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents. arXiv preprint arXiv:2402.01622v4.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset comprises 1,225 queries divided into training (45 pairs with human-annotated plans), validation (180 queries), and test (1,000 queries) sets. Queries are constructed by randomly selecting fundamental elements including departure city, destination, and specific date range to form the skeleton of each query. The duration of travel (3, 5, or 7 days) and the number of hard constraints are adjusted to create different levels of complexity.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Original data for tools is sourced from publicly available Internet data: FlightSearch data from Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset (2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01), DistanceMatrix from Google Distance Matrix API, RestaurantSearch from Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset, AttractionSearch from Google Places API, and AccommodationSearch from Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset. The data is then modified by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to avoid data contamination.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data spans from March 1, 2022 to April 1, 2022 for flight information. Other data collection timeframes are not explicitly specified.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: For FlightSearch, 'Price' is generated by multiplying 'Distance' by a random factor ranging from 0.2 to 0.5. For DistanceMatrix, 'Price' is calculated by multiplying 'Distance' by factors of 1 for self-driving and 0.15 for taxi modes.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Original data is modified by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values. Restaurants and accommodations are randomly assigned to various cities. Restaurants are randomly categorized under specific cuisines (Chinese, American, Italian, Mexican, Indian, Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, Korean, Asian, French). Accommodations are assigned random room rules (No parties, No smoking, No children under 10, No pets, No visitors).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: From FlightSearch dataset, specific fields are extracted: FlightDate, DepTime, ArrTime, ActualElapsedTime, Distance, OriginCityName, and DestCityName, while other values are discarded. For RestaurantSearch, Restaurant Name and Average Cost are extracted. For AttractionSearch, essential details retained include Name, Address, Phone, Website, Latitude, and Longitude. For AccommodationSearch, key details extracted include NAME, room type, price, minimum nights, review rate number, and maximum occupancy. Search results from APIs are stored in databases to create fixed datasets for evaluations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 20 graduate students meticulously annotated plans for synthesized queries. One plan is deemed eligible only if it meets all the constraints outlined in the evaluation script. The authors performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found. Budgets were re-calibrated using costs from corresponding human-annotated plans to replace initial heuristic-generated budgets. Multiple stages of human verification ensure high quality and the presence of at least one feasible solution for each query.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 is used for natural language query generation and key components extraction from plans
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current language agents are not yet capable of handling complex planning tasks in TravelPlanner—even GPT-4 only achieves a success rate of 0.6%. Language agents struggle to stay on task, use the right tools to collect information, or keep track of multiple constraints. Agents show substantial gaps between two-stage mode (tool-use and planning) and sole-planning mode. Agents struggle with global planning scenarios and fail to consider multiple constraints holistically. Common failure modes include argument errors in tool use, being trapped in dead loops, hallucinations, information confusion, and inability to align actions with reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of language agents' capabilities in complex planning tasks involving tool use, multi-constraint satisfaction, and long-horizon planning. The benchmark is designed to assess agents' performance in travel planning scenarios that require information collection, deliberation, and decision-making while satisfying explicit and implicit constraints.
